theron02.title: The Forgetting
theron02.t01: Someone paid well just to know a way through the old galleries. Whoever pays to know will one day pay to use.
theron02.d01: Was the door open? I lock everything. Everything. Wait there, I'm almost done.
theron02.e01.hint: The labyrinth's keeper lives by the Gate. Look around the house (E) before you talk to him.
theron02.h.keys.1: A board of bronze keys, each on a nail with a name scratched under it. One nail is empty. Beneath it, only: "Gate".
theron02.h.bread.1: A loaf wrapped in cloth, tied with a child's knot. Beside it, a small sandal. The keeper has a son who goes down into the galleries.
theron02.h.letter.1: A tablet with the seal of the Augural College: "The keeper answers with his life for any door opened without orders."
theron02.d02: If it's about the Gate, the answer is no. Nobody goes through. College orders.
theron02.d03: I don't want to go through. I only want to know where not to go, so I don't get lost.
theron02.c01: The keeper folds his arms. He's afraid, but not of you.
theron02.c01.son: Mention the son who goes down into the galleries.
theron02.c01.letter: Remind him of the College's letter.
theron02.d_silver: Silver doesn't buy what the College gives. The College gives fear, and fear lasts longer.
theron02.d_son: Don't talk about my son. He takes bread to... no one. He takes nothing to no one.
theron02.d_letter: You read the letter. Then you know: if I open my mouth, they shut it.
theron02.mthreads.hint: The threads that hold the keeper. Cut, loosen or tie.
theron02.mthreads.cut_filho: Cut the thread between Nísio and his son.
theron02.mthreads.loosen_filho: Loosened the thread of the son.
theron02.d_cut_dever: The Gate... The Gate stays where it is, it doesn't go anywhere. Why would I lock something that doesn't go anywhere? There, look: the old way runs through the cistern.
theron02.d_loosen_dever: A way? There's the cistern. No one uses it. I shouldn't say, but... who's going to ask?
theron02.d_cut_medo: The College? Let the College drown. You want ways? There's an old shrine of Hestia at the port. A door down there leads to a tunnel that runs under the Temple. It needs a key I don't have.
theron02.d_loosen_medo: Listen... there's a shrine of Hestia at the port. Old. They say a door down there leads to the galleries. But only with the goddess's key.
theron02.d_cut_filho: Son? I have no son. I've lived alone since... since always, I think. Is that bread yours? The way? Through the cistern. Take the bread too.
theron02.d_loosen_filho: My son... Take him away from here, if you can. Far from the Gate. I don't know why I'm telling you this.
theron02.d_tie: One day the keys will be my son's. That's how it must be: him and the Gate. The way? Through the cistern. He'll need to know it.
theron02.d_price1: ...and you are? Who let you in?
theron02.d_price2: The keeper looks at him as at a stranger. The whole conversation stayed on the other side, like a dream that leaves only a taste.
theron02.t_price: Always in the middle of a sentence. Every thread I touch takes a little of me with it.
theron02.d_press: No one will know you talked. I'm the man everyone forgets, remember? It's the one thing I do well.
theron02.d_words_ok: All right. All right! Through the old cistern. And never say it was me. No one would believe it anyway: I won't even remember your face.
theron02.d_words_fail: Out. Come back with an order from the College, or don't come back.
theron02.t_words: Words cost less. And buy less.
theron02.t_gift: He's afraid of something bigger than me. I could look at his threads and see what. And he would forget I was ever here.
theron02.t_gift.second: Every thread I touch takes a little of me with it. One day there will be no one left to touch anything.
theron02.gh: what binds the keeper to the Gate?
theron02.c_warn: On the way out, the bread tied with a child's knot. The keeper's son goes down into the galleries, and the College watches everything that goes down.
theron02.c_warn.warn: "Your son goes down into the galleries. Keep him home for a few days."
theron02.d_warn: Who sent you here? The College? ...What do you know about my son? Out. OUT.
theron02.t_port: The port, with silver at my belt. Eat, drink, vanish. In that order.
theron02.d_iante1: Sir. You look like someone who knows where to buy cheap medicine. My son has had a fever for nine days.
theron02.d_iante2: She has a Corinthian accent, a copper coin in her hand and a bronze key at her belt. The coin won't buy any medicine.
theron02.c_iante: She waits, coin held out, as if he were the apothecary.
theron02.c_iante.give: Give her the silver the way earned him.
theron02.c_iante.con: Offer a game of cups: "Double your coin."
theron02.d_give: ...Why? No one gives anything in this port. You... I will remember you. I swear I will.
theron02.d_con: Three rounds. The copper coin changes hands. She thanks him for the game, not understanding she lost, and goes back to asking the next man.
theron02.d_pass: He walks past. Behind him, she is already asking the next man.
theron02.h.colegio.1: A College scribe, tablet open, stops at every stall. He asks. No one answers. He writes it down anyway.
theron02.d_nw_cold: Yesterday you vanished into the crowd. Today you're back. Going to vanish again?
theron02.d_nw1: Théron. Sit. Your tunic is still torn, I saw it from here.
theron02.d_nw2: Early this morning, two men in white asked about a fellow in a torn tunic. I said I didn't know anyone like that. Yet.
theron02.t_nw: It may be nothing. Men in white ask about everyone.
theron02.t_nw.second: It may be everything. She is the only one who says my name out loud.
theron02.c_nerea: She goes back to her needle, waiting for his answer.
theron02.c_nerea.hide: "Disappear for a few days. Go mend somewhere far from here."
theron02.c_nerea.lie: "If they ask again, say you've never seen me."
theron02.d_hide: You show up once in a lifetime and it's to send me away. ...Fine. A few days. Then I come back, and you owe me a fish.
theron02.d_lie: Lying I can do. Forgetting you is what I never managed.
theron02.d_laugh: Laugh, laugh. Men in white don't laugh back.
theron02.t_end: A mother from Corinth, a name in a seamstress's mouth. Today I'm carrying more than I usually do.
